targets.authors: Leoutsakos JM, Forrester SN, Corcoran CD, et al.
targets.title: Latent classes of course in Alzheimer's disease and predictors: the Cache County Dementia Progression Study
targets.evidence_quote: In an attempt to increase our knowledge on the course of AD and its predictors, a prediction model based on data from the Cache County Dementia Progression Study (CCDPS) identified 4 different classes of cognitive and functional progression, with cognitive status at the moment of diagnosis being the strongest predictor of future decline. 8 Although replication is pivotal in prognostic factor research, 10 these findings have not been replicated yet. In the present study, we sought to replicate the prediction model from the CCDPS in a large clinical cohort from the National Alzheimer's Coordinating Center (NACC).
targets.outcome_quote: Although the identified classes in the present study are different from those identified in the CCDPS, the finding that the majority of the patients is a member of the class with relatively slow disease progression is consistent across cohorts.
targets.outcome_reasoning: The exact class structure explicitly failed replication, while slow progression in the majority and predictive ability agreed. Abstract confirmation concerns a specific predictive claim rather than an overall replication verdict. Other discussed trajectory studies are background comparisons, not designed targets.

reasoning: New clinical cohort tests the cited population-based CCDPS prediction model. Primary target is reference 8, not the later meeting abstract or measure sources.
